name: Range Resources Corporation
reason: Appalachian gas E&P whose earnings swing with natural gas prices (EBIT margin -43% to +55% over 10y, ROIC 10y avg 0.4%).

name: Edison International
reason: California wildfire liability (Eaton fire) and regulatory risk dominate, with net debt/EBITDA 4.9x, negative FCF conversion and EPS at 1.0x 10y max on adjusted basis.

name: Ingredion Incorporated
reason: Corn/tapioca starch and sweetener processor with 2.5% revenue CAGR and EPS at 1.0x 10y peak after a pricing run; input-cost driven and not special.

name: Encore Capital Group, Inc.
reason: Debt buyer whose returns depend on consumer credit cycles and portfolio pricing, with net debt/EBITDA 6.0x and EPS swinging to losses in 2023-24.

name: Arrow Electronics, Inc.
reason: Low-margin cyclical electronics distributor (3.0% EBIT margin) with EPS at 0.49x its 2022 peak and growth reliant on semiconductor cycle and buybacks.

name: East West Bancorp, Inc.
reason: Conservatively underwritten, efficient bank with 13.6% EPS CAGR, 15% avg ROE and negligible acquisitions; key risks to diligence are US-China exposure, CRE concentration and rate sensitivity.

name: Walt Disney Company
reason: Linear TV/ESPN in structural decline while streaming economics still maturing; EPS 10y CAGR only 1.4% and adjusted vs GAAP gap 95% make the earnings base hard to forecast despite great parks/IP.

name: Dynex Capital, Inc.
reason: Spread-dependent agency mortgage REIT with EPS -10.7%/yr over 10y and share count +21.7%/yr; earnings set by rates and hedging.

name: Enterprise Products Partners L.P.
reason: High-quality fee-based midstream MLP but EPS already 0.99x 10y max, LTG ~4% and leverage 3.6x; no plausible route to 7%+ EPS growth and partial NGL commodity exposure.

name: Brink's Company
reason: Cash-logistics business in secular cash decline whose growth came from acquisitions (acq/FCF 0.77) with adjusted EPS 131% above GAAP and margin at 10y high.

name: Royal Caribbean Group
reason: Best-in-class cruise operator but EPS and EBIT margin (27.6%) are both at 10y highs after the post-COVID rebound, with 3.2x leverage and a highly cyclical, shock-prone industry.

name: United Parcel Service, Inc.
reason: Parcel volumes deliberately shrinking from its largest customer (Amazon) with EPS at 0.55x its 2022 peak and 5y EPS CAGR of -2.7%.

name: Kroger Co.
reason: Ordinary low-margin grocer (3.2% EBIT margin, 3% revenue CAGR) whose EPS growth is mostly buybacks, facing Walmart/Costco/Amazon competition; cheap but not special.

name: Deluxe Corporation
reason: Check printer in secular decline using acquisitions (acq/FCF 0.93) to replace print, with EPS at 0.54x 10y peak and 3.0x leverage.

name: D.R. Horton, Inc.
reason: Largest US homebuilder with scale cost advantage, 0.6x net debt/EBITDA, 16.6% avg ROIC and 19% EPS CAGR; EPS at 0.7x 2022 peak with mid-cycle margins and a structural US housing shortage, though rate/cycle risk must be stress-tested.

name: Jones Lang LaSalle Incorporated
reason: Commercial real estate services earnings driven by capital-markets transaction activity (EPS halved in 2023) and EPS now 0.97x 10y max.

name: Stewart Information Services Corporation
reason: Sub-scale #4 title insurer tied to the housing transaction and mortgage-rate cycle, with acquisitions near 100% of FCF and EPS at 0.41x its 2021 peak.

name: Abercrombie & Fitch Co.
reason: Fashion apparel retailer after a sharp turnaround with EBIT margin at the 91st pctile of history and EPS 0.92x peak; fashion-cycle earnings are not forecastable.

name: Columbia Sportswear Company
reason: Ordinary outdoor apparel brand with EBIT margin at a 10y low (6.0%) and 4% revenue CAGR; cheap-ish but no moat or secular driver.

name: Whirlpool Corporation
reason: Commoditised appliance maker with net debt/EBITDA 6.1x, EPS at 0.23x its 10y peak and revenue shrinking 2.9%/yr.
